title: Normal finite-type models of finite semistable modification diagrams
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral affine scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain, and let $(C,D)$ be a multipointed $S$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Let $J$ be a finite set, and for each $j\in J$ let $f_j:(C_j,D_j)\to(C,D)$ be a semistable $\eta$-modification. Specify a subset $J_{\mathrm{st}}\subseteq J$ on which these modifications are stable. There exist a normal integral affine scheme $S_0$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a dominant map $S\to S_0$ taking generic point to generic point, a multipointed $S_0$-curve $(C_0,D_0)$ with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking, and semistable $\eta_0$-modifications $f_{j,0}:(C_{j,0},D_{j,0})\to(C_0,D_0)$, stable for $j\in J_{\mathrm{st}}$, such that their entire diagram of pairs pulls back [def-pc-fibre-product] to the given diagram over $S$. There is a dense open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ over whose preimage every $f_{j,0}$ is an isomorphism on both the curve and the marking. All the schemes $C_0,D_0,C_{j,0},D_{j,0}$ are reduced (their local rings have no nonzero nilpotents). A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text: Write S=Spec A, where A is an integrally closed domain. Use [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine]: the finitely generated Z-subalgebras A_i of A, ordered by inclusion, give S=lim S_i with S_i=Spec A_i and affine transition maps. The index set is nonempty (it contains the image of Z) and directed (adjoin the union of two finite generating sets). Every A_i is a domain because it is a subring of A. Thus every S_i is integral, and every projection S\to S_i takes generic point to generic point. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] the stages are Noetherian; they are affine, hence qcqs. This is a Noetherian approximation as in [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system].

source.place: Tag 01ZA, affine-case proof: filtered union of finitely generated subrings

proof.text: Every curve and marking object of the given finite diagram is finitely presented over S. Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to descend the objects at a common stage. Use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-diagram-lift-of-models] for the finite quiver consisting of the structure maps, marking inclusions and modification maps, with the finitely many relations expressing compatibility of each pair map. It supplies a common later stage, all arrows and relations, and comparison isomorphisms identifying the entire pulled-back diagram with the original diagram.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(1)--(3), finite collection of objects, arrows and equations

proof.text: Increase the stage so that every structural map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] and every marking map is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion]. The finite-presentation models are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; their marking and pair arrows are locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](f), since their composites to S_i are of finite presentation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] to the curve and marking arrows separately. Apply [lem-trf-pure-relative-dimension-finite-stage] to the structural maps with dimensions 1 and 0. After one common later stage all pairs are multipointed and all pair maps proper. [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change] preserve these properties under further base change.

source.place: Tags 04AI, 01ZP, 081F, 0EY2; finite-presentation hypotheses as in Situation 081D

proof.text: Put K_i=Frac(A_i) and K=Frac(A). Every fraction a/b in K belongs to K_i once A_i contains a and the nonzero b, so K is the directed union of the K_i, and Spec K=lim Spec K_i. Each generic pair map becomes an isomorphism over K. Apply the morphism and equality clauses of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the inverse maps over this field limit and their two inverse equations. Since there are finitely many maps, all generic fibres are isomorphisms at a common later stage i. The generic base pair over K_i pulls back to the given smooth curve and etale marking over K. [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] makes Spec K\to Spec K_i an affine flat surjection, hence an fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] and [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] to give smoothness and etaleness of that generic pair.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(2),(3) for the field system; descent Tags 02VL and 02VN

proof.text: Keep this stage i fixed. The principal localizations A_i[1/a] for nonzero a\in A_i form a directed system with colimit K_i. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2),(3) again to the generic inverse maps and their inverse equations in this system. The models are the restrictions of the already descended objects. A common nonzero a suffices for all maps and equations, yielding an open V_i=D(a) over which all curve and marking maps are isomorphisms. For any affine chart Spec B of any flat curve or marking, multiplication by a is injective by [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free], applied to the structure module on that chart. If b maps to zero in B[1/a], some a^n kills b, so b=0. Thus restriction to the preimage of V_i is injective on every affine chart and hence as a sheaf. These opens are schematically dense on both sources and targets. Each proper pair map is therefore an eta_i-modification.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(2),(3) for the principal-open system; explicit schematic-density argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-stable-modification-constructibility] to every pair map at this stage. Its base is integral Noetherian, all pairs multipointed, the maps proper, generic isomorphisms, and modifications by Step 5. It gives a constructible semistable set for every source and a constructible stable set for each selected arrow. Intersect these finitely many sets to get a constructible E\subset S_i; finite intersections are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Every point s of S maps into E: the fibre over s is obtained from the fibre over its image t by the field extension k(t)\subseteq k(s), and the given fibres are semistable and, when selected, stable. The equivalences in [lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-field-descent] imply the same properties at t. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible], a later stage S_h maps entirely into E. Thus [lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-field-descent] gives semistability of every source and stability of every selected arrow at S_h. Pull back V_i to V_h. It still contains the generic point and all maps are isomorphisms there; multipointedness, generic smoothness/etaleness, semistability and selected stability persist by [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change].

source.place: Remark 3.1.1(i),(ii), pp.14--15, and Lemma 5.1(ii), p.34; Stacks Tag 05F4

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-normal-finite-stage-universal] to the approximation of Step 1 and the stage h. It gives an integral normal S_0, finite over S_h, and a dominant S\to S_0 compatible with the projection. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], S_0 is affine and its ring is finite as an A_h-module. Module generators also generate it as an algebra, so S_0 is finite type over S_h and over Z by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both S\to S_0 and S_0\to S_h are dominant: the composite is the dominant projection and the first map is dominant; equivalently their affine ring maps are injective. They take generic point to generic point. Pull the whole diagram and V_h back to S_0, writing U_0 for that open. [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) preserves properness and closed immersions, while [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change] preserves all multipointed pairs, generic smoothness/etaleness, semistable sources and selected fibrewise stability. U_0 contains the generic point, hence is dense.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, normal Noetherian approximation paragraph; explicit affine finite-type refinement

proof.text: All generic curves are smooth: the base generic curve is smooth by Steps 4 and 7, and every other generic curve is isomorphic to it. All generic markings are etale by the corresponding generic isomorphisms, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] gives reduced generic fibres for all these objects. Write S_0=Spec A_0 with A_0 a domain. On any affine chart W=Spec B of a curve or marking, a nilpotent b maps to zero in B\otimes_{A_0}Frac(A_0), so some nonzero a\in A_0 kills b. By [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] on the flat chart W with its structure module, multiplication by a is injective, so b=0. Thus all the total spaces are reduced; this also covers empty markings or curves.

source.place: Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); the flat localization calculation is explicit

proof.text: The inverse image in S_0 of the principal open V_i=D(a) used in Step 5 is U_0. Its defining a remains nonzero because A_i\to A_0 is injective. On every affine chart of any flat curve or marking over S_0 the torsion-free-sections statement [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] again makes restriction to B[1/a] injective, by the element argument of Step 5. Thus the preimages of U_0 in both source and target are schematically dense; the proper maps, already isomorphisms there and generically, are eta_0-modifications. The semistable sources and selected fibrewise stability are exactly semistability and stability of these modifications. By fibre-product associativity from [def-pc-fibre-product], pulling the whole diagram back along S\to S_0 gives the original diagram. This proves all clauses, including a common dense open and reduced total spaces.
